items.title: SEM notice asking Neha Bora to sign peace bond not based on mere hearsay: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday observed that the show-cause notice issued by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) to All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 and maintain peace was not based on mere "hearsay". Justice Subramonium Prasad observed that the notice was based on the kalandara dated October 17, which consists of the three general diary entries registered at different Police Stations related to different dates and events. "As such, this Court cannot sit in the armchair of the SEM to test the subjective satisfaction of the sufficiency of material and as to whether the opinion has been correctly been arrived at by the SEM or not," the Bench said. The Court said that the notice, issued under Sections 126 and 130 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), met the legal requirements for initiating preventive proceedings. The High Court returned the finding as it dismissed Bora's plea against the notice. However, the Court directed the Police to provide all the material to Bora on which reliance will be placed at the time of enquiry and on which basis the notice has been issued.
